quiz.why: Addiction is a health condition, not a character flaw, and many people recover with support and treatment.
Withdrawal is feeling unwell (anxious, irritable, shaky or sick) when you stop using a substance the body has got used to.

lessons.title: Tobacco, vapes and alcohol: facts and law

scenes.text: Near Kunal's school, a shop sells loose cigarettes to schoolkids.
The school posts a sign quoting COTPA: no tobacco sale within 100 yards of educational institutions or to under-18s.
Parents report the shop. It stops.

steps.title: Tobacco
steps.body: India has one of the world's largest numbers of tobacco users. Smoking and smokeless tobacco (gutkha, khaini, zarda) cause cancers (especially mouth and lung), heart disease, stroke and lung disease. **COTPA 2003** bans: smoking in public places; sale to anyone **under 18**; sale within **100 yards of educational institutions**; tobacco advertising. Second-hand smoke harms others too.

steps.title: Vapes / e-cigarettes
steps.body: **Banned in India** (production, sale, import, advertising) under the **Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Act, 2019**. Most contain **nicotine**, highly addictive for teens; aerosols contain other harmful chemicals; flavours are designed to appeal to young people.

steps.title: Alcohol
steps.body: Alcohol slows the brain (it's a depressant): impairs judgement, coordination and memory; raises risk of accidents, violence, unsafe situations, and later liver disease and cancers. **Legal drinking age varies by state in India (often 21–25, and some states have prohibition)**. **Drink-driving** is an offence under the Motor Vehicles Act (blood alcohol limit 30 mg per 100 ml). Mixing alcohol with energy drinks or medicines is risky. Signs of alcohol poisoning: confusion, vomiting, slow/irregular breathing, can't be woken → **112**, keep them on their side, don't leave them.

steps.title: Solved example: the money check
steps.body:
A pack of 10 cigarettes ≈ ₹180 (prices vary). One pack a day for a year:
- 180 × 365 = **₹65,700** per year.
Over 10 years ≈ **₹6.5 lakh** — plus health costs.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- 'Hookah is just flavoured air' — it's tobacco smoke with carbon monoxide.
- 'Beer is not real alcohol' — it is.
- 'Coffee or a cold shower sobers you up' — only time does.

statements.s: E-cigarettes are banned in India.
Selling tobacco to under-18s is legal if parents allow.
Coffee sobers you up quickly.
Someone who can't be woken after drinking needs emergency help.
Gutkha is safer than cigarettes.

quiz.why: Under COTPA, selling tobacco products within 100 yards of schools and educational institutions is banned.
E-cigarettes are banned in India under the Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Act, 2019.
Alcohol is a depressant, as it slows the brain and body. It is not a stimulant, painkiller or vitamin.
An unconscious drunk person can choke and stop breathing. Put them in the recovery position, stay with them and call 112.

lessons.title: Cannabis, pills and other drugs: facts and the law

scenes.text: At a hostel party, Tara is offered a brownie 'with something extra'.
She remembers: cannabis can cause panic, paranoia, and is illegal under the NDPS Act.
'I'm good, thanks,' she says, and sticks with her friends who also refuse.

steps.title: Cannabis (ganja, charas, edibles)
steps.body: Affects memory, attention and coordination; can trigger anxiety, panic or paranoia; heavy teen use is linked to higher risk of psychosis in vulnerable people and to dependence. **Edibles** act slowly, so people take more and get overwhelmed. Under India's **NDPS Act 1985**, possessing, selling or using ganja and charas is an offence. (Bhang has a different legal status in some states — still not safe for teens.)

steps.title: Medicine misuse
steps.body: Taking someone else's prescription, or cough syrups, sleeping pills or painkillers in larger doses 'to feel high', is dangerous — risks include breathing problems, overdose and dependence. Some cough syrups containing codeine are regulated for this reason. Inhalants (glue, whitener, petrol) can cause sudden death even on first use.

steps.title: Other drugs
steps.body: Heroin ('smack', 'brown sugar'), cocaine, MDMA/ecstasy, methamphetamine and synthetic drugs carry high risks of addiction, overdose and mental-health harm, and are illegal. Drugs sold illegally are often **mixed with unknown substances**. Spiked drinks happen: keep your drink with you.

steps.title: Solved example: why edibles are risky
steps.body:
Smoke: effect in minutes. Edible: may take **30 min–2 hours**.
- A person feels nothing at 40 min, eats more, then both doses act together → overwhelming effects.
**Lesson:** delayed effect = higher risk of taking too much. (Best choice for teens: none at all.)

steps.title: General education
steps.body: This is general education, not legal advice. Laws can change — check current official sources.

activity.prompt: Sort the statement

items.text: Cannabis can trigger panic and paranoia
Prescription pills are always safe because doctors make them
Inhalants can cause sudden death even on first use
Illegal drugs are often mixed with unknown substances
You can't get addicted to cannabis

quiz.why: India's main drug law is the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. COTPA is about tobacco.

options: effects are delayed so people take more
quiz.why: Edibles (food with cannabis) act slowly, so people think nothing is happening and take more, which can lead to an overdose.
Inhalants like whitener fluid can cause sudden death, even on the first use, by affecting the heart and breathing.

quiz.q: Using someone else's prescription pills is…
quiz.why: Using someone else's prescription pills is dangerous, since the drug, the dose and the interactions may not suit you.
At parties, keep your drink with you and watch it, to avoid someone putting something in it (spiking).

lessons.title: Gaming, scrolling and saying no: refusal skills and getting help

scenes.text: Om plays online games till 3 am, skips meals and lies to his parents.
His grades fall; he snaps when asked to stop.
With his parents and a counsellor he sets limits, finds offline sports he enjoys, and keeps gaming to weekends.

steps.title: Behavioural addictions
steps.body: WHO recognises **gaming disorder**: impaired control over gaming, giving it increasing priority over other activities, continuing despite harm, for usually **12 months**. Not everyone who games a lot has it. Signs to watch for in gaming, scrolling or online betting: losing track of time, lying about use, irritability when stopping, dropping hobbies, sleep and grades suffering. **Online betting and gambling apps** can lead to serious debt — avoid them.

steps.title: Refusal skills
steps.body:
- **Say no clearly**: 'No thanks.'
- **Give a reason** (optional): 'I've got a match tomorrow.' 'My parents would kill me.' 'Not my thing.'
- **Suggest something else**: 'Let's get food instead.'
- **Walk away** and stick with friends who respect you.
- **Use an excuse** if you need: text a parent a code word to call you home.
Real friends accept 'no'.

steps.title: Solved example: screen-time budget
steps.body:
School day: 24 h − sleep 9 − school & travel 8 − homework 2 − meals & chores 2 = **3 h free**.
Goal: ≤1.5 h recreational screens, ≥1 h physical activity, rest for family/hobbies. Use the phone's screen-time limits and keep devices out of the bedroom at night.

steps.title: Getting help
steps.body: Talk to a trusted adult, school counsellor or doctor. **Tele-MANAS 14416** (mental health and substance use support). Government de-addiction services exist through district hospitals and the national drug-dependence treatment network, and the **national toll-free helpline for drug-abuse prevention, 14446**. In an overdose or poisoning: **112**.

a.text: At a friend's birthday, an older cousin offers you a beer: 'Come on, one won't hurt.'

choices.label: 'No thanks, I'm good.' Grab a soft drink and stay with friends
Say nothing and take it to avoid awkwardness
choices.feedback: Pressure often grows after the first yes.

b.text: Now they're offering something stronger, and a pill 'for fun'.

choices.label: Refuse firmly, text your parent the code word and leave
Try the pill
choices.feedback: Unknown pills can be very dangerous.

c.text: A friend who took the pill feels very unwell and is hard to wake.

choices.label: Call 112, put them on their side, stay with them

end1.text: Nobody made a big deal. Saying no early is easiest.

end2.text: You're safe. Next time you'll say no from the start.

options: impaired control and continuing despite harm
quiz.why: Gaming disorder (WHO) means impaired control over gaming and continuing despite harm. Liking games or owning a console is not a disorder.

options: say no clearly and suggest something else
quiz.why: A good refusal skill is to say no clearly and suggest something else to do. Long explanations or arguments give pressure room.
The drug-abuse prevention helpline (Nasha Mukt Bharat) is 14446.

quiz.q: Online betting apps can lead to…
quiz.why: Online betting apps can lead to serious debt and addiction, as the odds favour the house. They don't guarantee money.

quiz.q: A code word with parents helps you…
quiz.why: A code word agreed with parents lets you ask for help or leave an unsafe situation without having to explain in front of others.

questions.q: Dopamine is linked to…
questions.why: Dopamine is a brain chemical linked to reward and motivation. Addictive substances and habits trigger it strongly.

questions.q: E-cigarettes in India are…
questions.why: E-cigarettes are banned in India under the 2019 Act.

questions.q: Emergency number:
questions.why: 112 is the emergency number in India.

questions.q: Tobacco sale to under-18s is…
questions.why: Selling tobacco to anyone under 18 is prohibited under COTPA.

questions.q: Alcohol is a…
questions.why: Alcohol is a depressant: it slows the brain and nervous system.

questions.q: A refusal line:
questions.why: 'No thanks, not my thing' is a clear refusal. 'Maybe later' or silence invite more pressure.

questions.q: Assertion: Starting substances in teens raises addiction risk. Reason: The prefrontal cortex is still developing.
questions.why: Both are true. The prefrontal cortex, which controls decisions and impulses, is still developing in teens, so starting substances early raises addiction risk. The reason explains the assertion.

questions.q: India's main narcotics law:
questions.why: The main law on narcotics in India is the NDPS Act, 1985.

questions.q: Which is a withdrawal sign?
questions.why: Irritability when stopping is a withdrawal sign. Tolerance is needing more for the same effect.

questions.q: Case: A classmate smells of tobacco daily and coughs. Best supportive step?
options: Talk privately, share facts, suggest help
questions.why: Talk to the classmate privately, share facts about the harm, and suggest getting help. Mocking, ignoring or reporting to the police are not supportive.

questions.q: ₹200/day on cigarettes for a year =
Why do edibles lead to over-consumption?
questions.why: Edibles take a long time to work, so people think nothing is happening and take more doses, which leads to over-consumption.

questions.q: Drink-driving BAC limit in India (Motor Vehicles Act):
questions.why: Under the Motor Vehicles Act, the legal limit for driving is 30 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood.

questions.q: Case: A friend drank heavily, is vomiting and hard to wake. Correct action?
questions.why: A friend who drank heavily, is vomiting and hard to wake may have alcohol poisoning. Put them in the recovery position, stay with them and call 112.

questions.q: Which describes gaming disorder (WHO)?
options: Impaired control, priority over other life, continuing despite harm, usually ~12 months
questions.why: WHO describes gaming disorder as impaired control, giving gaming priority over other life activities, and continuing despite harm, usually for about 12 months.

questions.q: Free school day hours: 24 − sleep 9 − school 8 − homework 2.5 − meals 2 =
Which is the most effective first step for someone who wants to quit?
options: Tell a trusted adult/doctor and use support services like 14416 or 14446
questions.why: The best first step is to tell a trusted adult or doctor, and use support services like 14416 or 14446. Quitting alone in secret is harder, and switching to vapes is not a solution.

courses.title: Revision & Practice · Mind matters
courses.summary: Rapid revision of all mental-health units: key facts and skills, helplines, 'what would you do' cases, and a 20-question mock test.
outcomes: Learners can recall key facts and skills from every unit
Learners can choose safe, supportive actions in realistic cases
Learners can name the right help for each situation
courses.guardianNote: Revision of the mental-health units (stress, exams, anxiety, depression, self-harm safety, substances) with practice cases. Non-graphic, help-focused.

lessons.title: Key facts & skills sheet

scenes.text: Ira makes a small card for her wallet with coping skills and helpline numbers.
Her friends copy it.
Months later, one of them uses it to call 14416.

steps.title: Stress & coping
steps.body: Amygdala alarm → adrenaline & cortisol; parasympathetic calms. Tools: box breathing 4-4-4-4, 5-4-3-2-1 grounding, movement, sleep, STOP, thought-checking, problem-solving, self-compassion.

steps.title: Exams
steps.body: Active recall, spacing, interleaving, Pomodoro 25/5, realistic timetable with 8–10 h sleep, minutes per mark, I-statements for pressure, options map after results.

steps.title: Anxiety & depression
steps.body: Anxiety disorder = intense, long-lasting, disrupts life. Panic peaks ~10 min, passes; slow out-breath. Exposure ladder; worry time. Depression = 2+ weeks low mood/loss of interest + other changes; behavioural activation; therapy ± medicine; antidepressants not addictive.

steps.title: Safety & substances
steps.body: Self-harm = distress. Suicide warning signs: talk of burden/dying, goodbyes, giving away things, sudden calm. A-L-S-G. Safety plan. Tobacco (COTPA), e-cigs banned (2019), NDPS Act, alcohol depressant, gaming disorder. Numbers: **112**, **14416**, **1098**, **14446**.

cards.back: Review at growing gaps: 1 day, 3 days, 1 week…

quiz.why: Tele-MANAS is the free mental-health helpline, 14416. 112 is the emergency number, 14446 is the drug-abuse helpline and 1098 is Childline.
14446 is the Nasha Mukt Bharat helpline for drug-abuse prevention and help.
Exposure starts with the lowest-fear step and moves up gradually.
Behavioural activation means doing small, rewarding actions to lift mood, even when motivation is low.

lessons.title: Which help, when? Matching situations to support

scenes.text: The class draws a 'help map': which situations need a friend, an adult, a counsellor, a doctor or 112.
They argue about a few — and learn there's often more than one right answer.
The rule they agree on: when in doubt, tell an adult.

steps.title: Worked matches
steps.body:
- Mild stress before a test → self-help tools, friend.
- Low mood 3 weeks → trusted adult + counsellor/doctor.
- Panic attacks weekly → doctor/psychologist.
- Friend talking about suicide → adult now; 14416; 112 if immediate danger.
- Someone unconscious after drinking/drugs → 112.
- Under-18 being harmed → 1098.
- Wants to quit tobacco/drugs → doctor, 14416, 14446.

steps.title: Rule of thumb
steps.body: Danger to life now → **112**. Not sure → tell an adult. Need to talk → 14416 (24×7).

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body: Waiting for things to get 'bad enough'; handling a friend's crisis alone.

activity.prompt: Match the situation to the best first help
pairs: Feeling low for weeks and need to talk at night
A child is being hurt at home

quiz.why: If someone's life is in danger now, call 112, the emergency number.
If you are not sure what to do, tell an adult you trust. Don't keep it secret or post it online.
Weekly panic attacks need professional help, so see a doctor or psychologist. Avoiding everything or energy drinks makes it worse.
If a child is being harmed, call Childline on 1098.

lessons.title: Case practice: put it all together

scenes.text: Over one week, five friends each face something different.
The class works out what each could do.
Different problems, same pattern: notice, use a skill, reach out.

steps.title: Case A
steps.body: Meher blanks in the physics exam → pause, 3 slow breaths, start a known question, use minutes-per-mark.

steps.title: Case B
steps.body: Dev has stopped football and says he's 'useless' for a month → kindly ask, listen, encourage counsellor; tell an adult.

steps.title: Case C
steps.body: Ali is pressured to vape behind the canteen → 'No thanks', walk away with friends; vapes are banned and nicotine is addictive.

steps.title: Case D
steps.body: Priya says goodbye to friends and gives away her diary → warning signs; A-L-S-G; adult now; 14416/112.

statements.s: In Case D, waiting until tomorrow is fine.
Dev's month-long low mood is worth professional help.
Meher should leave the exam hall.
Saying 'No thanks' and walking away is a valid refusal.

options: notice, use a skill, reach out
quiz.why: A common pattern across the unit: notice what is happening, use a coping skill, and reach out to someone for support.
When a friend shows signs of immediate risk (Case D), tell an adult now and call 14416 or 112. Waiting or joking is unsafe.
The fact for Case C: vapes (e-cigarettes) are banned in India. They are not vitamins, water or legal.
In Case A (anxiety or panic), the first step is slow breaths, which calm the body. Leaving or copying doesn't solve it.

questions.q: Fight-or-flight hormone:
questions.why: Adrenaline, released by the adrenal glands, is the fight-or-flight hormone.

questions.q: Tele-MANAS:
questions.why: Tele-MANAS is 14416.

questions.q: Self-harm is a sign of…
questions.why: Self-harm is a sign of distress, a way of coping with emotional pain. It needs care.

questions.q: E-cigarettes in India:
questions.why: E-cigarettes are banned in India under the 2019 Act.

questions.q: Spaced practice:
questions.why: Spaced practice means reviewing material at growing gaps, which helps long-term memory.

questions.q: Panic attack peaks within about…
questions.why: A panic attack usually peaks within about 10 minutes.

questions.q: Depression duration:
questions.why: Depression involves symptoms lasting 2 weeks or more.

questions.q: A refusal line:
questions.why: 'No thanks.' is a clear, short refusal that holds your ground.

questions.q: Assertion: Avoidance maintains anxiety. Reason: The brain doesn't learn the situation is safe.
questions.why: Both are true. Avoiding a feared situation prevents the brain from learning that it is safe, so anxiety continues. The reason explains the assertion.

questions.q: Which is a thinking trap?
questions.why: Catastrophising, imagining the worst, is a thinking trap. Box breathing, problem-solving and sleep are helpful.

questions.q: Alcohol is a…
questions.why: Alcohol is a depressant, as it slows the brain. It is not a vitamin, antidepressant or stimulant.

questions.q: Asking about suicide directly:
options: helps open the door to support
questions.why: Asking directly about suicide helps open the door to support and does not plant the idea.

questions.q: 90 marks, 180 min, 15 min reading time: minutes per mark?
questions.why: Time to write = 180 − 15 = 165 minutes. 165 ÷ 90 marks ≈ 1.83, which is about 1.8 minutes per mark.

questions.q: Mood rises 3→5, 2→3, 4→6: average rise?
questions.why: The rises are 2, 1 and 2, so the average = (2 + 1 + 2)/3 = 5/3 ≈ 1.67.

questions.q: ₹120/day habit for a year:
Case: Friend with fear of lifts. First exposure step?
options: Look at a lift from outside
questions.why: Exposure starts with the least scary step, such as looking at a lift from outside. Riding to the 30th floor alone is too big a jump, and avoiding lifts keeps the fear.

questions.q: Case: Friend says they've 'made a plan' to end their life. Correct?
questions.why: A friend who has 'made a plan' to end their life is in danger. Stay with them, get an adult immediately and call 112. Promising secrecy or waiting can cost a life.

questions.q: Case: Unconscious after drinking. Correct?
questions.why: A person who is unconscious after drinking should be placed in the recovery position. Stay with them and call 112. Cold showers and coffee don't help and leaving them is dangerous.

questions.q: Which reflects behavioural activation?
options: Planning a 10-minute walk even without motivation
questions.why: Behavioural activation means planning a small activity, such as a 10-minute walk, even without motivation. Waiting, sleeping more or avoiding friends keeps mood low.

questions.q: Why is 'sudden calm' after deep depression a concern?
options: Can follow a decision to end life
questions.why: A sudden calm after deep depression can sometimes follow a decision to end life. It should not be assumed to be recovery, so it needs a check-in.

well-puberty-2.title: Puberty in depth: growing up, for every body
well-puberty-2.description: A detailed, judgment-free guide to puberty for girls and boys: periods and period care, nocturnal emissions, body image, hygiene and myths — medically accurate and non-explicit.

courses.title: Unit 1 · Puberty: the big picture for everyone
courses.summary: What puberty is, the hormones that run it, the typical timeline for girls and boys, growth spurts and why everyone develops at their own pace — for every child, whatever their body.
outcomes: Learners can explain what puberty is and why it happens
Learners can name the hormones and glands involved
Learners can describe typical ages and order of changes in girls and boys
Learners can explain why early and late development are both normal and when to check with a doctor
courses.guardianNote: Explains puberty changes for all genders in calm, medically accurate, non-explicit language (no images beyond emoji), following UNESCO ITGSE 2018 guidance for ages 9–15. It helps children understand their bodies before changes happen and know which trusted adults to ask. Parents may like to go through it together.

lessons.title: What puberty is — and why it happens

scenes.text: In the Class 6 photo, some kids are suddenly tall, some look the same as in Class 4.
Ishan, the shortest, feels left behind. Pari, the tallest, feels awkward.
Their teacher: 'Puberty is a train everyone boards — just at different stations.'

steps.title: Puberty in plain words
steps.body: **Puberty** is the time when a child's body gradually becomes an adult body that could, one day, make a baby. It usually takes **3–5 years**. The emotional and social changes that come with it are called **adolescence** (roughly 10–19 years, as WHO describes it).

steps.title: Who switches it on?
steps.body:
1. The **hypothalamus** in the brain starts releasing a signal hormone (GnRH) in pulses.
2. The **pituitary gland** responds with **FSH** and **LH**.
3. These reach the **ovaries** (which make **oestrogen** and **progesterone**) or the **testes** (which make **testosterone**).
4. These sex hormones cause most of the body changes. The adrenal glands also add hormones that cause body odour, oily skin and some hair growth.

steps.title: Changes that happen to everyone
steps.body: Growth spurt · sweat and body odour · oily skin and pimples · hair under the arms and in the pubic area · stronger feelings and mood swings · new interest in privacy, friendships and sometimes crushes · thinking skills develop — the brain keeps maturing into the mid-20s.

steps.title: Solved example: why is it gradual?
steps.body:
Q: Why don't changes happen overnight?
- Step 1: Hormone levels rise slowly over years.
- Step 2: Different tissues respond at different hormone levels (e.g. breast buds or testicle growth early; adult height later).
- **So:** puberty is a sequence, not a switch.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- 'Puberty is an illness' — it is normal growth.
- 'Something is wrong if my friend started and I didn't' — a range of several years is normal.
- 'Only girls go through puberty' — everyone does.

activity.prompt: Put the hormone chain in order

quiz.why: Puberty usually takes about 3–5 years to complete, although it starts at different ages for different children.

quiz.q: FSH and LH come from the…
quiz.why: FSH and LH, the hormones that trigger puberty changes in the ovaries and testes, are made by the pituitary gland.

quiz.q: Testosterone is made mainly in the…
quiz.why: Testosterone is made mainly in the testes in boys, and it drives changes like a deeper voice and facial hair.
Body odour (from active sweat glands) happens to everyone in puberty. Periods, breast growth and facial hair are not the same for all.

quiz.q: Adolescence according to WHO is about…
quiz.why: WHO defines adolescence as the period from 10 to 19 years of age.

lessons.title: The typical timeline: girls and boys

scenes.text: Twins Riya and Rohan are both 11.
Riya has grown 7 cm this year; Rohan hasn't changed yet.
Their doctor: 'Girls often start 1–2 years earlier. Rohan's spurt will come — and he'll likely end up taller.'

steps.title: Girls (typical, with wide normal range)
steps.body:
- Starts about **8–13 years** with **breast buds** (small, sometimes tender bumps under the nipple; one side may start first).
- Pubic and underarm hair; growth spurt (peak around 11–12).
- Hips widen; body shape changes; vaginal discharge (clear/white) begins.
- **First period (menarche)** usually **about 2–3 years after breast buds**, commonly between **10 and 15** (often around 12–13).

steps.title: Boys (typical, with wide normal range)
steps.body:
- Starts about **9–14 years** with the **testicles getting larger** (often unnoticed), then the penis grows.
- Pubic and underarm hair; growth spurt (peak around 13–14, later than girls).
- Voice 'cracks' then deepens; facial hair; shoulders broaden; muscles grow.
- Erections become more frequent; first ejaculation often during sleep (**nocturnal emission / wet dream**), often around 12–15.

steps.title: Solved example: compare the timing
steps.body:
Girl A: breast buds at 9.5 → expected first period ≈ 9.5 + 2 to 3 = **11.5–12.5 years**.
Girl B: breast buds at 12 → ≈ **14–15 years**.
Both normal. Boy C: testicles enlarge at 12 → peak growth spurt might be around 14.

steps.title: When to check with a doctor
steps.body:
- Signs of puberty **before 8 (girls)** or **before 9 (boys)**.
- **No breast development by 13**, or **no period by 15**.
- **No testicle enlargement by 14** in boys.
- Growth that suddenly stops, or changes that are very rapid.
These are reasons for a check-up, not panic — many have simple explanations.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Comparing yourself to the fastest friend.
- 'Late bloomers end up shorter' — not necessarily.
- 'Girls stop growing at first period' — most grow a few more centimetres (often ~5–7 cm) afterwards.

activity.prompt: Which change is typical for whom? (Some happen to both!)

quiz.q: The first sign of puberty in most girls:
quiz.why: In most girls, the first sign of puberty is breast buds, small tender lumps under the nipples.

quiz.q: The first sign in most boys:
quiz.why: In most boys, the first sign of puberty is enlargement of the testicles, which is often unnoticed.

quiz.q: A girl's first period usually comes…
quiz.why: A girl's first period usually comes about 2–3 years after the breast buds appear.

options: a good reason for a doctor's check-up
quiz.why: If there is no period by age 15 (or no breast development by 13), it is a good reason for a doctor's check-up, though often the cause is harmless.
Girls usually start puberty about 1–2 years earlier than boys, so their growth spurt also comes earlier.

lessons.title: Growth spurts, sleep and food

scenes.text: Thirteen-year-old Aman eats two lunches and is still hungry.
His trousers are short again — 9 cm in a year!
His mother notices he needs more sleep too. 'Your body is building,' she says.

steps.title: The spurt
steps.body: During the peak of the growth spurt, many teens grow around **6–10 cm in a year**. Hands and feet often grow first (feeling 'clumsy' is common), then arms and legs, then the trunk. Bones grow at **growth plates** near their ends, which close after puberty — after that, height stops increasing.

steps.title: Fuel for growth
steps.body: Regular meals with protein (dal, eggs, milk, paneer, soy, fish, meat), calcium (milk, curd, ragi, sesame), iron (green leafy vegetables, pulses, jaggery, meat) with vitamin C, plenty of fruit and vegetables. Teen girls need extra iron once periods start. No 'height-increase' powder or pill has good evidence — be wary of ads.

steps.title: Solved example: growth arithmetic
steps.body:
Sana was 142 cm at 11 and 150 cm at 12.
- Growth = 150 − 142 = **8 cm/year** → she's likely near her peak growth velocity.

Second: Om grew 4 cm between 10 and 11 and 9 cm between 13 and 14 → his spurt came later — normal for boys.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Dieting during the growth spurt — can slow growth and harm periods and bones.
- 'Hanging from bars adds height' — it's good exercise but doesn't change final height.
- Skipping sleep — growth hormone is released mostly in deep sleep.

activity.prompt: Leela was 138 cm on her 10th birthday and 145 cm on her 11th. How many cm did she grow that year?

quiz.why: Height growth happens at the growth plates, soft areas near the ends of long bones. They close at the end of puberty.

quiz.q: During the spurt, teens may grow about…
quiz.why: During the growth spurt, teens may grow about 6–10 cm a year.
Height pills sold online lack good evidence, so they should not be trusted. Good food, sleep and activity support healthy growth.

quiz.q: Girls need extra ___ once periods start
quiz.why: Once periods start, girls lose some iron in menstrual blood, so they need extra iron from foods like greens, pulses and jaggery.

quiz.q: Feeling clumsy during the spurt is…
quiz.why: Feeling clumsy during the growth spurt is common, as hands and feet often grow first and the brain needs time to adjust.

lessons.title: Feelings, privacy and the teenage brain

scenes.text: Kavya, 12, starts closing her door and wants to change in private.
Some days she snaps at her little brother for nothing, then feels guilty.
Her father knocks first now, and they agree on 'talk time' after dinner.

steps.title: Why moods swing
steps.body: Hormone changes, a brain that is still wiring its 'brake' system (the **prefrontal cortex** matures last, into the mid-20s), less sleep, and more pressure from school and friends can make feelings stronger and faster. This is normal. Persistent sadness or worry for **2 weeks or more** is different — tell someone.

steps.title: Privacy is a right
steps.body: Wanting privacy while changing, bathing or using the toilet is healthy. Everyone — including family — should **knock and ask**. Your body belongs to you: no one should touch your private parts or ask to see or photograph them, except a parent or doctor for a health reason, with you knowing why. If anyone does, it is **not your fault**; tell a trusted adult or call **1098**.

steps.title: Solved example: handling a mood spike
steps.body:
Kavya snapped at her brother.
- Step 1: Notice — 'I'm irritated and tired.'
- Step 2: Pause — 5 slow breaths or a short walk.
- Step 3: Repair — 'Sorry I snapped; I'm tired. Not your fault.'
- Step 4: Prevent — earlier bedtime, snack after school.

steps.title: Your trusted-adult list
steps.body: Pick at least **3 adults** you can ask about body changes or problems — e.g. a parent, an aunt/uncle, a school counsellor or nurse, a doctor. If one isn't helpful, ask the next.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- 'Feelings mean I'm crazy' — no; they're signals.
- Keeping secrets that make you feel unsafe — safe secrets don't make you scared.

activity.prompt: Write the names of three trusted adults you could talk to about body changes, and one question you'd like to ask.
activity.hint: Think of someone at home, someone at school, and one more (relative, doctor, counsellor).

quiz.q: The brain area that matures last:
quiz.why: The prefrontal cortex (for planning and self-control) is the last brain area to mature, around the mid-20s.
Sadness on most days for 2 weeks or more is more than a mood swing. Tell a trusted adult, as support can help.

quiz.q: Knocking before entering a room is about…
quiz.why: Knocking before entering a room is about respecting privacy, which matters more as bodies change.

quiz.q: If someone touches your private parts without a health reason…
options: tell a trusted adult or call 1098
quiz.why: If someone touches your private parts without a health reason, it is never your fault. Tell a trusted adult or call Childline 1098, and do not keep it secret.
Childline in India is 1098, a free helpline for children.

questions.q: Puberty is…
options: normal growth into an adult body
questions.why: Puberty is the normal growth into an adult body. It is not an illness, and it happens to everyone.

questions.q: Oestrogen is made mainly by the…
questions.why: Oestrogen, the main female sex hormone in puberty, is made mainly by the ovaries.

questions.q: Childline number in India:
questions.why: Childline in India is 1098.

questions.q: Which change happens to all genders?
questions.why: A growth spurt happens in all genders. A beard, periods and breast milk are not shared by all.

questions.q: A boy's first sign of puberty is usually…
questions.why: In most boys, the first sign of puberty is growth of the testicles.

questions.q: Typical age range for menarche:
questions.why: The first period (menarche) usually happens between about 10 and 15 years of age.

questions.q: Assertion: Girls' growth spurt usually comes earlier than boys'. Reason: Girls usually begin puberty earlier.
questions.why: Both are true. Girls usually begin puberty earlier than boys, so their growth spurt also comes earlier. The reason explains the assertion.

questions.q: Which hormone chain is right?
questions.why: The hormone chain begins in the hypothalamus, which signals the pituitary gland, which then signals the ovaries or testes.

questions.q: Which is a reason to see a doctor?
questions.why: No breast development by age 13 is a reason to see a doctor, as it may mean delayed puberty. A voice crack at 14, pimples and a period at 12 are normal.

questions.q: Case: Sunil, 13, grows 2 cm while friends grow 8 cm. He's healthy and his testicles have just started enlarging. Best view?
options: Likely normal timing; his spurt may come later
questions.why: Sunil has only just begun puberty, so his growth spurt (which in boys comes later in puberty) will likely come later. This is a normal variation in timing.

questions.q: Breast buds at 10.5. Estimated first period window (2–3 years later):
questions.why: A first period usually comes 2–3 years after breast buds. 10.5 + 2 = 12.5 and 10.5 + 3 = 13.5, so the window is 12.5–13.5 years.

questions.q: 130 cm at 11, 139 cm at 12. Growth rate:
questions.why: Growth rate = 139 − 130 = 9 cm in one year, i.e. 9 cm/year, typical of a growth spurt.

questions.q: Why do teenagers' moods swing more?
options: Hormones, a still-maturing prefrontal cortex, less sleep and more stress
questions.why: Teen moods swing because of hormone changes, a still-maturing prefrontal cortex, less sleep and more stress. It is not a choice or laziness.

questions.q: After growth plates close…
questions.why: When the growth plates close at the end of puberty, bones can no longer lengthen, so height growth stops.

questions.q: Case: An 11-year-old girl's adult cousin asks to see 'how she's developing' and says not to tell. Best response?
options: Say no, leave, and tell a trusted adult or call 1098
questions.why: Asking to see how a child is developing, and telling her to keep it secret, is unsafe. Say no, leave, and tell a trusted adult or call Childline 1098. It is never her fault.

questions.q: Which statement is MOST accurate?
options: A wide range of starting ages is normal, with doctor checks for very early or very late signs
questions.why: A wide range of starting ages is normal, so a doctor check is needed only for very early or very late signs. Early or late starters are not unhealthy, and late starters do not stay short.

questions.q: Which is the best evidence-based advice for growing teens?
options: Regular balanced meals, 8–10 h sleep, daily activity
questions.why: Healthy growth is supported by regular balanced meals, 8–10 hours of sleep and daily activity. Energy drinks, height powders and skipping meals do not help.

courses.title: Unit 2 · Growing up as a girl: breasts, periods & period care in depth
courses.summary: Everything a girl needs to know before and after her first period: breast development and bras, how the menstrual cycle works, a first-period kit, every period product and safe disposal, cramps and PMS, irregular periods, PCOS awareness, and busting myths.
outcomes: Learners can describe breast development and choose comfortable support
Learners can explain the menstrual cycle with hormones and phases
Learners can prepare a period kit and use pads, cups, tampons and cloth safely
Learners can manage cramps and PMS and know when to see a doctor
Learners can respectfully correct common period myths
courses.guardianNote: Covers breast development, the menstrual cycle, first period preparation, all period products and disposal, cramps, PMS, irregular cycles and PCOS awareness, in medically accurate, non-explicit, judgment-free language (UNESCO ITGSE 2018; WHO). Suitable for girls 9+ and useful for boys and parents too, so periods are understood rather than whispered about.

lessons.title: Breast development and bras

scenes.text: Nisha, 10, notices a small, slightly sore bump under one nipple and fears something is wrong.
Her mother explains these are breast buds — and it's common for one side to start first.
A few months later they pick a soft cotton 'starter' bra together.

steps.title: How breasts develop
steps.body: Breast buds appear first (often tender; one side may be ahead). Over **3–5 years** breasts grow, the area around the nipple (areola) may darken and widen. It is very common for breasts to be **different sizes** — even in adults. Size has nothing to do with health, feeding a baby later, or worth.

steps.title: Bras: optional comfort
steps.body: A bra isn't medically required. Many girls like a soft **cotton starter bra or sports bra** for comfort, during sport, or under thin uniforms. Fit: band snug but not tight, straps not digging, no gaping. Sizes change often during puberty — re-check every few months.

steps.title: Solved example: is this normal?
steps.body:
(a) Left breast slightly bigger at 11 → **normal**.
(b) Small bumps around the areola → **normal** glands.
(c) Fine stretch marks on breasts or hips during growth → **normal**, fade with time.
(d) A hard lump that keeps growing, nipple discharge with blood, or skin dimpling → **see a doctor** (rare in teens and usually benign, but should be checked).

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Strapping breasts flat to hide them — can cause pain and skin problems.
- Thinking small or big breasts mean anything about health.
- Laughing at someone's development — it hurts; it's also a form of harassment.

statements.s: It's normal for one breast bud to appear before the other.
Every girl must wear a bra from age 10.
Breasts of slightly different sizes are normal.
A painful growing lump with bloody discharge should be checked by a doctor.

quiz.why: Breast buds are often tender at first, as the tissue starts to grow. This is normal and not a sign of illness.
Breast development takes about 3–5 years to complete, so it is a gradual process.
A starter bra is an optional comfort, not a medical need. Wear one if you feel more comfortable, especially for sport.
It is common for breasts to be slightly different in size. Differences are usually small and often even out.
Binding breasts tightly can cause pain, skin problems and breathing difficulty. It does not make them stop growing, so it is best avoided.

lessons.title: The menstrual cycle explained

scenes.text: Meera's aunt, a nurse, draws a big circle on a paper calendar.
'Every month your body prepares in case of a pregnancy. If there isn't one, the lining leaves — that's your period.'
'So a period means my body is working normally?' 'Exactly.'

steps.title: The organs
steps.body: Two **ovaries** (store egg cells — a girl is born with all of them), two **fallopian tubes**, the **uterus** (womb — a hollow muscular organ about the size of a fist, pear-shaped), the **cervix** (neck of the uterus) and the **vagina** (the passage to the outside). The **vulva** is the outer area. Correct names help you talk to doctors clearly.

steps.title: The four phases (example 28-day cycle)
steps.body:
1. **Menstruation (days 1–5ish)**: the uterus lining sheds as period blood.
2. **Follicular phase**: FSH helps an egg mature; **oestrogen** rebuilds the lining.
3. **Ovulation (around day 14 in a 28-day cycle)**: an **LH surge** releases an egg into the tube.
4. **Luteal phase**: **progesterone** keeps the lining ready. No pregnancy → hormones fall → next period.

Day 1 = first day of bleeding. Ovulation happens about **14 days before** the next period, so in a 32-day cycle it's around day 18.

steps.title: What's typical
steps.body:
- Period lasts **2–7 days**.
- Total blood loss usually about **30–40 ml** (a few tablespoons) — looks like more because it's mixed with tissue and fluid.
- In the **first 2–3 years**, cycles of **21–45 days** and some irregularity are common; adults are usually 21–35 days.
- Colour from bright red to brown; small clots can be normal.

steps.title: Solved example: predict the next period
steps.body:
Last period started **3 March**; cycle ≈ 30 days.
- 3 March + 30 days = **2 April**.
- Estimated ovulation ≈ 14 days before = **19 March** (rough guide only).

Second: cycle lengths 28, 34, 31 → average (28+34+31)/3 = **31 days**.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- 'You lose litres of blood' — it's a few tablespoons.
- 'Ovulation is always day 14' — only in a 28-day cycle, and it varies.
- Counting the cycle from the last day of bleeding — always count from **day 1 of bleeding**.
- Period-tracking apps predict, they don't guarantee.

activity.prompt: Order the cycle phases starting from day 1
items: Ovulation: LH surge releases an egg
Hormones fall and the next period begins

quiz.why: Day 1 of the menstrual cycle is the first day of bleeding.

quiz.q: Ovulation is triggered by a surge of…
quiz.why: Ovulation (release of an egg) is triggered by a surge of LH (luteinising hormone) from the pituitary gland.

quiz.q: Typical total blood loss per period:
quiz.why: The usual total blood loss in a period is about 30–40 ml, a few tablespoons, spread over several days.

quiz.q: In a 30-day cycle, ovulation is around day…
quiz.why: Ovulation happens about 14 days before the next period. In a 30-day cycle, that is about day 30 − 14 = day 16.

quiz.q: In the first years, cycles of 21–45 days are…
quiz.why: In the first years after periods start, cycles of 21–45 days are common and normal, as the hormones are still settling.

lessons.title: Your first period: be ready

scenes.text: During maths, Aditi feels wetness and finds a red-brown spot on her skirt at break.
Her friend Fatima hands her a pad from her 'just-in-case' pouch and ties a sweater round her waist.
The school nurse helps, and Aditi messages her mum: 'It came!' Her mum replies with a hug emoji.

steps.title: What it's like
steps.body: The first period is often light — a few spots of red, pink or brown in your underwear — and may not come again for a couple of months. Some girls feel mild cramps, a heavy feeling, or nothing at all. It is a normal sign of health, not something to be ashamed of.

steps.title: The 'just-in-case' kit
steps.body: Keep a small pouch in your school bag: **2–3 pads**, a clean pair of **underwear**, a small **paper bag** or newspaper for wrapping used pads, **wipes or tissues**, and maybe a dark-coloured spare pair of shorts. Tie a jacket round your waist if you have a stain — it happens to almost everyone at some point.

steps.title: Solved example: using a pad step by step
steps.body:
1. Wash hands.
2. Peel the backing and stick the pad to the **inside of your underwear** (wings fold under, if it has them).
3. Change every **4–6 hours** (sooner if heavy) — even if it's not full, for hygiene and to prevent rashes.
4. Used pad: roll it up, wrap in its wrapper or paper, put it in a **bin** — never flush.
5. Wash hands again.

steps.title: Who to tell at school
steps.body: A female teacher, the school nurse/counsellor or a friend. Many Indian schools now keep pads and sanitary-pad vending machines or incinerators. If you're a boy and a classmate has a stain — quietly tell her or lend your sweater. That's kindness, not a joke.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Waiting until the pad is full to change it.
- Using the same cloth or pad all day.
- Flushing pads (blocks toilets).
- Feeling you must hide it from your parents — most are glad to help.

activity.prompt: Pack my just-in-case period kit
items: Paper bag or newspaper for wrapping
Name of a teacher or nurse I can go to

options: light, with spots of red or brown
quiz.why: A first period is often light, with spots of red or brown blood. It is not always painful or heavy.
Change a pad about every 4–6 hours, to stay comfortable and prevent skin irritation and infection.
Wrap used pads in paper and put them in a bin. Flushing blocks drains, and burning plastic pollutes.

quiz.q: If a classmate has a stain, the kind thing is to…
options: quietly tell her or lend a sweater
quiz.why: Quietly telling the classmate or lending her a sweater is kind. Laughing or sharing it embarrasses her.

quiz.q: Is it normal for the second period to come 2 months later?
options: Yes, in the first year irregular cycles are common
quiz.why: Yes, in the first year, cycles are often irregular, so a second period 2 months later can be normal. It does not mean pregnancy.

lessons.title: Period products: pads, cloth, cups, tampons & period underwear

scenes.text: At a pharmacy, Juhi, 14, sees shelves of pads, cups, tampons and 'period panties'.
'Which is best?' she asks the pharmacist.
'The one that suits your body, budget, comfort and access to water and disposal. Let me explain each.'

steps.title: Disposable pads
steps.body: Easiest to start with. Choose by flow (regular, heavy, overnight). Change every **4–6 h**. Wrap and bin. Unscented pads may irritate skin less.

steps.title: Reusable cloth pads
steps.body: Low cost and less waste. **Wash in cold water first, then soap; dry fully in direct sunlight** (sunlight helps kill germs; damp cloth grows germs), store in a clean dry place. Change every 4–6 h. Replace when worn. Never use dirty or damp cloth — it can cause infections.

steps.title: Menstrual cups
steps.body: A soft medical-grade silicone cup folded and placed inside the vagina; it collects blood. Empty and rinse every **4–12 hours** depending on flow and the maker's instructions; **boil to sterilise** between periods. Many teens can use them; it can take a few cycles to learn. Using a cup or tampon does **not** affect virginity — that's a social idea, not a medical one.

steps.title: Tampons & period underwear
steps.body: **Tampons**: small absorbent plugs placed in the vagina; use the **lowest absorbency** you need; change every **4–8 hours, never more than 8**. Rarely, leaving tampons in too long is linked to **toxic shock syndrome (TSS)** — sudden high fever, rash, vomiting, dizziness → remove and seek urgent care. **Period underwear**: absorbent pants; rinse cold and wash per label.

steps.title: Solved example: cost over a year
steps.body:
Disposable pads: ~₹8 per pad × 4 pads/day × 5 days × 12 months = **₹1,920/year**.
A cup costing ₹600 lasting several years → about **₹120–200/year**.
Cloth pads: a set of 6 at ₹600 lasting ~2 years → **₹300/year**.
(Prices vary — the method of calculation is what matters.)

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Leaving a tampon in overnight beyond 8 hours.
- Drying cloth pads hidden indoors in the dark.
- Thinking cups or tampons can get 'lost inside' — the cervix closes the top of the vagina; they can't travel into the body. If you can't remove one, stay calm, relax, or see a doctor.

activity.prompt: Match the product to the key safety rule
pairs: Change every 4–6 hours, wrap and bin
Wash and dry fully in sunlight
Empty within the maker's limit; boil between periods
Lowest absorbency; never more than 8 hours
Rinse cold and wash as labelled

quiz.why: Cloth pads should be washed well and dried in direct sunlight. Sunlight helps kill germs, and damp cloth can cause infection.

quiz.q: Tampons should never stay in longer than…
quiz.why: A tampon should be changed at least every 8 hours, as leaving it in longer raises the risk of toxic shock syndrome, a rare but serious illness.
Menstrual cups are sterilised by boiling in water between periods.

quiz.q: Using a tampon or cup affects virginity?
options: No — that's a social idea, not medical
quiz.why: No. Using a tampon or cup does not affect 'virginity'. Virginity is a social idea, not a medical state.

quiz.q: Sudden high fever, rash, vomiting with a tampon in →
options: remove it and seek urgent care
quiz.why: High fever, rash and vomiting while using a tampon can be toxic shock syndrome (TSS), a rare but serious illness. Remove the tampon and get urgent medical care; adding another or waiting could be dangerous.

lessons.title: Cramps, PMS, irregular periods, PCOS — and myths

scenes.text: Every month Simran, 15, misses a day of school with cramps.
Her doctor suggests a heat pad, light exercise and a painkiller at the right dose at the start of cramps.
She tracks her cycle and now plans ahead. The doctor says to return if pain gets worse or periods become very heavy.

steps.title: Cramps (dysmenorrhoea)
steps.body: Caused by **prostaglandins** that make the uterus muscle contract. Help: hot water bottle or heat pad on the lower tummy, gentle exercise or yoga, warm drinks, rest. Painkillers like **ibuprofen** (if no stomach or asthma problems) or **paracetamol**, at the dose on the label or as advised, often work best started early. See a doctor if pain stops you from daily life despite this.

steps.title: PMS
steps.body: **Premenstrual symptoms** in the days before a period: bloating, breast tenderness, mood changes, tiredness, cravings, pimples. Regular sleep, exercise, less salt and caffeine, and tracking help. Severe mood symptoms that disrupt life (PMDD) need a doctor.

steps.title: When to see a doctor
steps.body:
- **Heavy bleeding**: soaking a pad every 1–2 hours, periods over 7 days, large clots, dizziness.
- **No period by 15**, or periods stopping for **3+ months** after being regular.
- Cycles shorter than 21 or longer than 45 days that continue after the first 2–3 years.
- Severe pain.
- **PCOS awareness**: irregular or missed periods, acne, extra hair on face/body, weight gain — PCOS (polycystic ovary syndrome) is common and **manageable** with medical help.

steps.title: Solved example: track and spot a pattern
steps.body:
Cycle start dates: 2 Jan, 9 Feb, 30 Mar, 21 May (age 16).
- Lengths: 38, 49, 52 days → over 45 and getting longer → **book a check-up** (could be PCOS, thyroid, stress, weight changes or other causes).

steps.title: Myths vs facts
steps.body:
Many families have customs around periods — respect your family while knowing the medical facts:
- Periods do **not** make anyone impure or unclean.
- You **can** bathe and wash your hair (warm baths can ease cramps), exercise, swim with a tampon or cup, go to school, cook, and eat any food including pickles and curd.
- Period blood is not 'dirty blood' — it's blood and uterine lining.
- Boys should learn about periods too.

activity.prompt: Period questions girls often don't ask

items.q: Can I swim on my period?
items.a: Yes, with a tampon or cup. Pads don't work in water.

items.q: Is brown blood normal?
items.a: Yes — it's older blood, common at the start or end of a period.

items.q: Can I get pregnant on my period?
items.a: It's less likely but possible, especially with short cycles, because sperm can survive several days. This matters for older teens and adults.

items.q: Does exercise make cramps worse?
items.a: Usually the opposite — gentle movement often helps.

items.q: Why do I get pimples before my period?
items.a: Hormone shifts increase oil production. Gentle skin care helps.

items.q: My friend's period lasts 3 days, mine 6. Is that OK?
items.a: Yes, 2–7 days is normal.

quiz.why: Period cramps happen because the womb lining releases prostaglandins, chemicals that make the uterus muscle contract. It is a body process, not caused by cold water, food or anything you did wrong.
Soaking through a pad every 1–2 hours means very heavy bleeding, which can lead to tiredness or anaemia, so see a doctor. A 3-day period, brown blood at the end and mild cramps are all common.

quiz.q: Can you bathe and wash hair on your period?
quiz.why: Yes, bathing and washing hair is safe and healthy during periods, and it helps you feel fresh. Water temperature and the day of the period make no difference; this is a myth.
PCOS (polycystic ovary syndrome) is a hormone condition whose common signs are irregular periods, acne and extra facial or body hair. Toothache, sneezing and short sight are unrelated.
Average = total ÷ number of cycles. 25 + 28 + 31 = 84, and 84 ÷ 3 = 28 days.

questions.q: Day 1 of the cycle is the…
questions.why: By rule, cycle day 1 is the first day of bleeding, because the period marks the start of a new cycle. Ovulation comes much later, about the middle of the cycle.

questions.q: A period usually lasts…
questions.why: A period usually lasts about 2–7 days. One month or 15 days is far too long, and one hour is too short.

questions.q: Used pads go…
questions.why: Used pads should be wrapped in paper and put in a bin. Flushing blocks toilets, and leaving them outside spreads germs and harms the environment.

questions.q: Ovaries make…
questions.why: The ovaries make the female hormones oestrogen and progesterone, which run the menstrual cycle. Insulin comes from the pancreas and bile from the liver.

questions.q: The womb is the…
questions.why: The womb is the medical name for the uterus, where the lining builds up each month and where a baby grows in pregnancy. The vagina is the passage, and ovaries make eggs.

questions.q: Cloth pads must be…
questions.why: Cloth pads must be washed and dried fully in sunlight, because sun helps kill germs. Damp, shared or unwashed pads can cause infection.

questions.q: Assertion: Ovulation happens about 14 days before the next period. Reason: The luteal phase is fairly constant at about 14 days.
questions.why: Both are true and R explains A. The luteal phase after ovulation stays fairly constant at about 14 days, so ovulation falls about 14 days before the next period, even when cycle length varies.

questions.q: Tampon maximum wear time:
questions.why: A tampon should be changed at least every 8 hours. Wearing one longer raises the risk of infection, including toxic shock syndrome.

questions.q: Which is a myth?
questions.why: Saying periods make girls impure is a myth with no scientific basis; a period is a normal body process. The other statements are true.

questions.q: Case: A 13-year-old's periods came at 30 and then 42 days apart. Best view?
options: Common in the first years; keep tracking
questions.why: In the first few years after periods start, cycles are often uneven because hormones are still settling. So gaps of 30 and 42 days are common; keep tracking and see a doctor only if worried or it persists.

questions.q: Last period began 10 June; cycle 32 days. Next expected:
questions.why: Next period = start date + cycle length. 10 June + 32 days: 20 days to 30 June, then 12 more gives 12 July.

questions.q: Cycle of 35 days: approximate ovulation day:
questions.why: Ovulation happens about 14 days before the next period. So for a 35-day cycle, 35 − 14 = day 21, not day 14, which only fits a 28-day cycle.

questions.q: Pads at ₹6 each, 5 per day, 5 days, 12 months. Yearly cost:
questions.why: Pads per year = 5 per day × 5 days × 12 months = 300 pads. Then 300 × ₹6 = ₹1,800.

questions.q: Which sign most needs a doctor?
options: Soaking a pad every hour with dizziness
questions.why: Soaking a pad every hour with dizziness is very heavy bleeding with possible blood loss, so it needs a doctor. Mild cramps, a 30-day cycle and pre-period pimples are normal.

questions.q: Case: Fever 39.5 °C, rash and vomiting, tampon in for 10 hours. Correct action?
options: Remove tampon and seek urgent medical care
questions.why: Fever, rash, vomiting and a tampon left in 10 hours point to possible toxic shock syndrome, an emergency. Remove the tampon and get urgent medical care; resting or inserting a new one is dangerous.

questions.q: Case: At 16, cycles are 50–60 days, with acne and new chin hair. Most sensible step?
options: See a doctor — possible PCOS or hormone issue
questions.why: Cycles of 50–60 days with acne and new chin hair can signal PCOS or another hormone problem. A doctor can check and treat it, so ignoring it as normal is not wise.

questions.q: Why is period blood loss usually smaller than it looks?
options: It's mixed with tissue and fluid; actual blood ~30–40 ml
questions.why: The fluid you see is blood mixed with tissue from the womb lining and other fluid, so the actual blood lost is only about 30–40 ml. That is why it looks like more than it really is.

courses.title: Unit 3 · Growing up as a boy: voice, hair, erections & wet dreams in depth
courses.summary: A calm, complete guide to boys' puberty: how the testes and penis develop, voice breaking, facial and body hair and shaving, spontaneous erections, nocturnal emissions (nightfall) and the myths around them, temporary chest swelling, and genital hygiene and testicle safety.
outcomes: Learners can describe the male reproductive organs with correct names and what changes at puberty
Learners can explain voice change and shave safely if they choose
Learners can explain erections and wet dreams as normal and harmless
Learners can reject myths about semen loss and 'weakness'
Learners can practise genital hygiene and recognise testicle emergencies
courses.guardianNote: Covers boys' puberty: genital growth, voice, hair and shaving, erections, nocturnal emissions (wet dreams), temporary chest changes, genital hygiene and testicle safety, in calm, medically accurate, non-explicit language (UNESCO ITGSE 2018). It also corrects harmful myths about semen loss that cause needless anxiety. Useful for girls and parents too.

lessons.title: What changes: testes, penis and sperm

scenes.text: In Class 7, Mr. Thakur keeps an anonymous question box.
One note reads: 'Why does one testicle hang lower? Is it normal?'
He answers calmly for the whole class: 'Yes, very normal — usually the left hangs a bit lower.'

steps.title: The organs (correct names)
steps.body:
- **Testes (testicles)**: two oval glands in a skin pouch, the **scrotum**. From puberty they make **sperm** (millions each day) and **testosterone**. They sit outside the body because sperm develop best slightly below body temperature.
- **Epididymis**: coiled tube on each testis where sperm mature.
- **Vas deferens (sperm ducts)**: carry sperm upward.
- **Seminal vesicles & prostate gland**: add fluid → together with sperm this is **semen**.
- **Urethra**: tube through the **penis** that carries urine *or* semen (never both at once).

steps.title: What changes, and when
steps.body: Testicles enlarge first (about 9–14 years), then the scrotum skin darkens and loosens, then the penis grows longer and wider over several years; pubic hair appears. Growth often continues until about 17–18. One testicle hanging lower, and differences in size and shape between people, are **normal**. Penis size varies a lot and has nothing to do with masculinity or health.

steps.title: Solved example: sperm and temperature
steps.body:
Q: Why does the scrotum hang loose on hot days and pull up when cold?
- Step 1: Sperm production needs about **2–3 °C below** core body temperature.
- Step 2: Muscles in the scrotum relax in heat (testes move away from body) and contract in cold (testes move closer).
- **Conclusion:** it's a built-in thermostat.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Comparing size with friends or online videos — online material is not realistic and often harmful.
- 'Bigger testicles/penis = stronger man' — false.
- Being ashamed to ask a doctor — doctors see these questions every day.

activity.prompt: Match the organ to its job
pairs: Holds testes at a cooler temperature

quiz.why: Sperm are made in the testes (testicles). The prostate adds fluid to semen, while the bladder and kidneys deal with urine.

quiz.q: Testes are outside the body because…
quiz.why: Sperm develop best at a temperature slightly lower than the body's, which is why the testes hang outside the body in the scrotum.
It is normal for one testicle to hang lower than the other; this is very common and not a disease.
Semen is sperm mixed with fluids from glands such as the prostate and seminal vesicles. It is not urine, sweat or blood.

quiz.q: Penis size is linked to masculinity?
quiz.why: No. Penis size has nothing to do with being masculine or with health or worth. Believing it does is a myth.

lessons.title: Voice, hair and shaving

scenes.text: Reciting a poem, Faizan's voice cracks high in the middle of a line.
Some classmates giggle. His teacher says, 'That's his voice growing up — it happens to most boys.'
At home his father shows him how to shave his fuzzy moustache safely, if he wants to.

steps.title: Voice breaking
steps.body: Testosterone makes the **larynx (voice box)** grow and the **vocal cords** lengthen and thicken, so the voice deepens. For a few months it may crack or wobble. The larger larynx may show as an **Adam's apple**. Girls' voices deepen slightly too. Singers: keep singing gently within a comfortable range; don't strain.

steps.title: Hair
steps.body: Order is often: pubic hair → underarm → upper lip → chin and cheeks → chest/legs (varies, and genes decide how much). Some men have lots of body hair, some very little — both normal. Facial hair may keep filling in until the 20s.

steps.title: Solved example: shave step by step (if you choose to)
steps.body:
1. Wash face with warm water to soften hair.
2. Apply shaving gel/foam.
3. Use a **clean, sharp razor**; shave **in the direction hair grows** first, light strokes.
4. Rinse blade often.
5. Rinse face with cool water; pat dry; apply a fragrance-free moisturiser.
6. **Never share razors** (risk of infections like hepatitis B).
Tip: electric trimmers cause fewer cuts and bumps.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- 'Shaving makes hair grow back thicker/darker' — myth; cut hair just feels blunt.
- Shaving dry, or pressing hard — causes cuts and razor bumps.
- Teasing someone about voice cracks — everyone goes through it.

activity.prompt: Put the shaving steps in order
items: Shave gently in the direction of hair growth
Rinse face with cool water and moisturise

quiz.why: In puberty the larynx (voice box) and vocal cords grow larger and thicker, which makes the voice deeper. Teeth, tongue and lungs are not the cause.

quiz.q: Shaving makes hair grow back thicker?
quiz.why: Shaving does not change how thick hair grows. It only cuts hair at the surface, and the blunt tip just feels coarser as it grows back.
Razors can carry tiny amounts of blood, so sharing them can spread blood-borne infections like hepatitis B. Asthma and rickets do not spread this way.

options: with the direction of hair growth
quiz.why: Shaving with the direction of hair growth causes less irritation and fewer cuts. Dry shaving, pressing hard against the grain or using a rusty blade can hurt the skin or cause infection.
Voice cracking is temporary and usually lasts some months while the voice box adjusts. It does not last forever.

lessons.title: Erections and wet dreams (nightfall) — completely normal

scenes.text: Varun, 13, wakes up to find his shorts and sheet damp and sticky.
He panics: 'Am I sick? Did I wet the bed?' He searches online and sees scary claims about 'losing strength'.
His uncle, a doctor, explains: 'It's a nocturnal emission — a wet dream. It's normal, healthy and doesn't weaken you at all.'

steps.title: Nocturnal emission (wet dream / nightfall)
steps.body: During sleep the body may release **semen** from the penis — a **nocturnal emission**. It often happens during dreams (not always sexual, and you may not remember). It is the body's natural way of starting and regulating sperm release. Some boys have them often, some rarely, some never — **all normal**. It is **not** bedwetting and not a sign of illness.

steps.title: Erections
steps.body: An **erection** is when spongy tissue in the penis fills with blood so it becomes firm. During puberty, erections often happen **for no reason** — when nervous, in class, on waking ('morning wood'), or while sleeping (several times a night). They go away on their own in a few minutes. Tips: think about something else, sit, carry your bag in front, wear supportive underwear.

steps.title: Solved example: what to do after a wet dream
steps.body:
1. It's fine — no one needs to know unless you want to tell.
2. Wipe or wash with water; change into clean underwear.
3. Put sheets/clothes to wash (or rinse the spot).
4. Carry on with your day — nothing has been 'lost'.

Semen is made continuously; the body replaces it. The amount is small (a teaspoon or so).

steps.title: Myths that cause needless fear
steps.body: In South Asia some people believe semen loss causes weakness, poor memory, hair fall or 'dhat' illness. **Medical evidence does not support this.** Wet dreams and semen release do not cause weakness, shrink muscles, damage eyesight or reduce height. Be wary of clinics, roadside 'sex specialists' or ads selling medicines to 'stop nightfall' — they profit from fear. If anxiety about this affects your sleep or mood, talk to a qualified doctor or call **14416**.

steps.title: Also normal
steps.body: Some people touch their own genitals in private for pleasure (masturbation). It is common in all genders, it does not cause physical harm, and it's equally fine not to. It belongs in private, and should never involve anyone else who hasn't agreed, or anyone under 18 with an adult.

activity.prompt: Wet-dream questions boys rarely ask out loud

items.q: Did I wet the bed?
items.a: No. Semen is thicker and different from urine. It's a nocturnal emission.

items.q: Will it make me weak?
items.a: No. That's a myth. Your body keeps making semen and nothing is lost.

items.q: Can I stop them?
items.a: You don't need to. They usually become less frequent with age.

items.q: I never have them. Am I abnormal?
items.a: No. Many boys never or rarely have them.

items.q: Should I tell my parents?
items.a: Only if you want to. You can wash your own sheets. A father, uncle or doctor can answer questions.

items.q: Why do I get erections in class?
items.a: Hormones cause random erections in puberty. They pass in minutes — think of something else.

quiz.why: A wet dream (nocturnal emission) is a normal release of semen during sleep in puberty. It is not an illness and is different from bedwetting, which is urine.
Medical evidence shows that losing semen does not cause weakness. The idea is a myth; the body keeps making semen and sperm.

options: normal and pass on their own
quiz.why: Random erections are normal in puberty because of changing hormones. They happen at any time and pass on their own.

quiz.q: After a wet dream you should…
options: wash and change; nothing to worry about
quiz.why: A wet dream is normal, so just wash and change clothes. No tablets or doctor visit are needed.

quiz.q: Ads selling pills to stop nightfall…
quiz.why: Ads for pills to stop nightfall play on fear of something normal to sell products. Wet dreams need no treatment, so be wary of such ads.

lessons.title: Chest changes, body image and comparison

scenes.text: Ankit, 13, notices a tender, slightly swollen area under one nipple and starts wearing two T-shirts in PE.
He worries he's 'turning into a girl' after a classmate's joke.
His doctor explains temporary breast-tissue swelling is very common in boys during puberty and usually settles within months to 2 years.

steps.title: Gynaecomastia in puberty
steps.body: Many boys (often quoted as up to half or more) get a small, sometimes tender lump of breast tissue under one or both nipples in puberty, due to a temporary hormone balance shift. It **usually goes away on its own** within months to about 2 years. See a doctor if it's large, very painful, growing fast, one-sided and hard, or there's nipple discharge.

steps.title: Muscles come later
steps.body: Muscle bulk increases mostly in the **later** part of puberty as testosterone rises. Building strength with bodyweight exercises, sport and good food is great. **Protein powders aren't needed** for most teens who eat a balanced diet; **anabolic steroids** and 'testosterone boosters' are dangerous for teens.

steps.title: Solved example: talking back to a mean joke
steps.body:
Joke: 'Ankit has man-boobs!'
- Option 1 (calm): 'It's puberty. Happens to loads of guys.'
- Option 2 (boundary): 'Not funny. Stop.'
- Option 3: tell a teacher if it continues — that's **body-shaming**, a form of bullying.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Comparing your body with filtered online images or adult athletes.
- Starving or over-exercising to 'fix' your body.
- Taking supplements from gyms without a doctor.

statements.s: Breast-tissue swelling in boys during puberty is common and usually temporary.
Teens need protein powder to build muscle.
statements.why: A balanced diet is enough for most.

statements.s: Anabolic steroids are safe for teen athletes.
Muscle bulk mostly grows in later puberty.

quiz.why: Some boys get chest swelling in puberty because of hormone changes. It usually goes away on its own, so it does not need surgery and is not a sign of illness.
Most muscle growth in boys comes later in puberty, as testosterone rises. So being slim early on is not a problem.

quiz.q: A body-shaming joke is a form of…
quiz.why: Making jokes that shame someone's body is bullying because it hurts and humiliates them, even if it is meant as fun.

quiz.q: See a doctor for a chest lump if…
options: it's hard, growing fast or has discharge
quiz.why: A hard lump, fast growth or discharge are warning signs that need a doctor. A small, tender swelling is common in puberty.
Testosterone boosters are risky for teens because they interfere with natural hormones and can cause lasting harm. They are not vitamins and are not needed.

lessons.title: Genital hygiene and testicle safety

scenes.text: During a match, a ball hits Pranav hard between the legs.
The pain is awful but fades in 20 minutes.
His coach explains: 'Pain that fades is usually OK. But sudden severe pain without injury, or pain that doesn't settle — that's an emergency.'

steps.title: Daily hygiene
steps.body:
- Wash the genital area daily with water and mild soap; rinse and dry well.
- If you are **uncircumcised**: once the foreskin can move back naturally (often by the teens — never force it), gently pull it back, rinse underneath with water, then return it forward. This removes **smegma**, a natural whitish build-up.
- Clean cotton underwear daily; change after sport.
- Wear a cup/box guard for cricket and contact sports.

steps.title: Testicular torsion — an emergency
steps.body: **Sudden, severe pain in one testicle**, often with swelling, nausea or vomiting, sometimes waking you from sleep, can mean the testicle has **twisted** and cut off its blood supply. It's most common in teens. **Go to hospital / call 112 at once** — surgery within about **6 hours** gives the best chance of saving the testicle. Don't let embarrassment delay you.

steps.title: Self-check in later teens
steps.body: From about 15–16, some doctors suggest occasionally checking testicles in a warm shower for any **new hard lump** or change in size. Testicular cancer is rare but most common in young men aged 15–35, and very treatable when found early. Bumps at the top-back (epididymis) are normal — ask a doctor if unsure.

steps.title: Solved example: urgent or not?
steps.body:
(a) Ball hit, pain eases in 30 min, no swelling → **rest, ice wrapped in cloth**; doctor if not better.
(b) Woke at 3 am with severe pain on one side and vomiting → **emergency now**.
(c) Itchy red rash in groin after sports → likely fungal; keep dry, see a doctor.
(d) Pain or burning when urinating → see a doctor.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Forcing back a tight foreskin in young boys — can cause injury; ask a doctor if it's tight in the teens.
- Waiting till morning with sudden severe testicle pain.
- Using harsh soaps or powders on genitals.

a.text: You wake at night with sudden, severe pain in one testicle. There was no injury. You feel sick.

choices.label: Wake a parent and go to hospital now
choices.feedback: Correct — possible torsion is an emergency.

choices.label: Wait till morning; it's embarrassing

b.text: An hour later the pain is worse and your scrotum is swelling.

choices.label: Tell a parent now and call 112

end1.text: Doctors check and treat you fast. Embarrassment fades; a quick decision protects your health.

quiz.q: Sudden severe testicle pain without injury →
quiz.why: Sudden severe testicle pain without injury may be testicular torsion, where the testicle twists and loses blood supply. It is an emergency, so go to hospital now; waiting can lose the testicle.

quiz.q: Surgery for torsion is best within about…
quiz.why: Torsion cuts off blood flow, so surgery works best within about 6 hours. After that the testicle may be permanently damaged.

options: a natural build-up under the foreskin
quiz.why: Smegma is a natural build-up of dead skin and oils under the foreskin. It is harmless and is removed by gentle rinsing with water.

quiz.q: A tight foreskin in a young child should…
quiz.why: A tight foreskin in a young child should never be forced back, since that can cause pain, tearing and scarring. It loosens naturally with time.

quiz.q: Testicular cancer is most common at…
quiz.why: Testicular cancer is most common in young men aged about 15–35, which is why knowing what is normal and checking early matters. It is rare in small children and in very old age.

questions.q: Sperm are made in the…
questions.why: Sperm are made in the testes. The prostate adds fluid to semen, while the bladder and kidney handle urine.

questions.q: A wet dream is…
questions.why: A wet dream is a normal release of semen during sleep in puberty. It is not a disease and is not bedwetting.

questions.q: Never share…
questions.why: Never share razors, because they can carry blood and spread infections such as hepatitis B. Sharing ideas and books is fine.

questions.q: The voice deepens because the…
questions.why: The voice deepens because the larynx (voice box) grows and the vocal cords lengthen under hormones. Lungs do not shrink, and the heart or nose are not involved.

questions.q: Random erections during puberty…
questions.why: Random erections are normal in puberty because of hormone changes. They are not rare, not permanent and not a sign of illness; they pass.

questions.q: Chest swelling in teen boys usually…
questions.why: Chest swelling in teen boys (gynaecomastia) is caused by hormone changes and usually settles by itself. It is not cancer and rarely needs surgery.

questions.q: Assertion: Testes hang outside the body. Reason: Sperm develop best slightly below body temperature.
questions.why: Both are true and R explains A. Sperm develop best slightly below body temperature, so the testes hang outside the body in the scrotum.

questions.q: Which is a myth?
questions.why: Semen loss causing weakness is a myth. The other statements are true: torsion is an emergency, hormones change the voice, and wet dreams are normal.

questions.q: Order of fluid path for sperm:
questions.why: Sperm are made in the testis, stored in the epididymis, travel through the vas deferens and leave through the urethra. The other orders are anatomically wrong.

questions.q: Case: A boy's friend says, 'Shaving makes beards thicker, so shave daily from 12.' Correct reply?
options: It's a myth — shaving doesn't change thickness
questions.why: Shaving does not change how thick hair grows, so the claim is a myth. Starting daily shaving at 12 gives no benefit, and razors should never be shared.

questions.q: Case: 2 am, sudden severe one-sided testicle pain and vomiting. Best action?
questions.why: Sudden severe one-sided testicle pain with vomiting suggests torsion, a surgical emergency. Go to hospital immediately; painkillers, ice or waiting may cost the testicle.

questions.q: Why are teens advised not to use anabolic steroids?
options: They disrupt natural hormones and can cause lasting harm
questions.why: Anabolic steroids upset the body's natural hormones and can cause lasting harm in teens, such as stunted growth, heart and liver problems. That is the main reason to avoid them.

questions.q: A 'clinic' advertises a ₹5,000 cure for nightfall weakness. Best judgement?
options: It exploits a myth; nightfall is normal; see a qualified doctor if worried
questions.why: Nightfall is normal, so a costly cure for it exploits a myth and fear. If you are worried, see a qualified doctor rather than paying for such a clinic.

questions.q: Which hygiene advice is correct for an uncircumcised teen?
options: Force the foreskin back daily from infancy
Gently retract once it moves naturally, rinse, then return it
questions.why: The foreskin should never be forced. Once it retracts easily by itself, gently pull it back, rinse with water, and return it. Strong antiseptics irritate, and never washing causes build-up.

questions.q: Which statement is MOST accurate?
options: All boys have wet dreams weekly
Frequency varies widely; none, rare or frequent are all normal
questions.why: Wet dream frequency varies widely, and having none, few or many are all normal. They do not mean anything about pornography and do not stop growth.

questions.q: Case: A 16-year-old feels a new hard, painless lump on one testicle. Best step?
options: Ignore; cancer only in old men
questions.why: A new hard, painless testicular lump could be a sign of testicular cancer, which is most common in young men. See a doctor soon, because early checking leads to better results.

questions.q: The scrotum pulling up in cold is an example of…
questions.why: In cold the scrotum pulls the testes closer to the body to keep them warm, and in heat it relaxes. This keeps temperature right for sperm production; it is normal, not fear or illness.

courses.title: Unit 4 · Body image, comparison & feeling at home in your body
courses.summary: Why changing bodies can feel strange, how filters and ads distort what 'normal' looks like, handling comments about weight, height, skin colour or shape, a healthy relationship with food and movement, and recognising when worries about food or body need help.
